title: I used Claude Code and Codex to make a slime roguelite. It's on Steam now.
author: schoolbus11
selftext:
I released Mool: Chroma this week. It's a slime roguelite built with Phaser and JavaScript. You eat colors and mix them to change your attacks.



I used Claude Code first, then Codex. They helped with programming, fixes and getting the Steam builds ready. The pixel art is drawn by code when the game starts, and the sound and music use Web Audio.



The part that kept coming back was testing. Save loading, controller input and language switching all went through several rounds of fixes before release. A clean test run still didn't replace opening the actual game and checking it.



AI also helped with some writing and translations, and with this post. The shipped art and sound don't use generative image or audio models, and nothing is generated live during play.



The clip is from the full game. There's a free demo with the first two stages for Windows and Mac:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5156510/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5156510/)



I'd really appreciate it if you gave it a try and let me know what you think.
